recipes.title: Pudina Hilsa (Mint Fish)
recipes.description: Bengali hilsa baked in butter with mint, ginger paste, green chilli, capsicum and nutmeg.

steps.instructionText: Wash the hilsa fish pieces thoroughly in water.
Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F).
In a baking dish, mix the salt, sugar, 25 g of the butter, pudina, ginger paste, nutmeg, capsicum and green chilli paste.
Add the hilsa pieces, coat them in the mixture and dot the rest of the butter on top.
Bake at 200 °C (400 °F) until the fish turns golden and is cooked through. Serve hot with boiled rice.

recipes.title: Sprouted Moong Chutney
recipes.description: Fiery raw chutney of sprouted green moong ground with ginger and green chillies, sharpened with lemon.

steps.instructionText: Soak the green moong in water for 3-4 hours, then drain and leave it to sprout.
Mince the green chillies and ginger with a little salt.
Grind the sprouted moong, chillies and ginger to a paste in a mortar and pestle or food processor.
Season with lemon juice to taste and serve.

recipes.title: Sindhi Rajma
recipes.description: Kidney beans simmered with fried onion, tomato and chillies, finished with garam masala and pepper.

steps.instructionText: Soak the rajma in water overnight, then drain.
Cover the rajma with fresh water, add the baking soda and boil briskly for at least 30 minutes, until tender.
Drain, keeping back 100 ml of the cooking water.
Fry the onion in a little oil until golden brown.
Add the tomato and green chillies and fry until the oil separates.
Add the rajma and the reserved cooking water and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the salt and red chilli powder.
Take off the heat and mix in the garam masala and black pepper. Serve hot with roti or rice.

recipes.title: Rasmalai
recipes.description: Soft paneer discs poached in sugar syrup, then soaked in chilled, cardamom-scented reduced milk.

steps.instructionText: Crumble the paneer, add 2 tbsp of the maida and knead with your palm into a smooth dough.
Divide into 16 equal portions, roll into balls and press them slightly to flatten.
Thinly slice the almonds and pistachios.
Dissolve 2 cups of the sugar in the water and bring to the boil.
Slowly lower the paneer balls into the boiling syrup and cook on high heat for 10 minutes.
Sprinkle in a little water and the remaining 1/2 tbsp maida, bring back to the boil and cook for a few minutes more.
Meanwhile, boil the milk in a heavy pan, then lower the heat and keep boiling until it reduces to a third of its volume.
Add the rest of the sugar and the cardamom powder and boil until the sugar dissolves. Cool, then refrigerate for 1 hour.
Mix the almonds and pistachios into the milk.
Gently squeeze the paneer balls and add them to the chilled milk. Refrigerate for 30 more minutes and serve chilled.

recipes.title: Sai Bhaji
recipes.description: Sindhi chana dal cooked with spinach, methi, dill and vegetables, finished with a garlic tadka.

steps.instructionText: Soak the chana dal overnight, then drain and put it in a pot.
Add the ginger and green chillies, cover with water and boil for at least 5 minutes, until the dal is tender. Drain.
Heat some oil in a large pan. Add the methi, palak, suva, tomatoes, brinjals, potatoes and bhindi.
Cook, stirring now and then, until the greens are well wilted and the vegetables are soft.
In a small pan, fry the garlic in a little oil until golden. Stir in the salt, turmeric and red chilli powder.
Stir the garlic mixture and the dal into the vegetables and serve hot.

recipes.title: Kerala Sambar (Roasted Coconut)
recipes.description: Toor dal and vegetable sambar thickened with coconut roasted dark with chilli and coriander.

steps.instructionText: Wash the toor dal and cook it in water until soft, then mash it.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a pan. Fry the hing, red chilli powder, coriander powder and whole dhania well.
Add the coconut and fry until the mixture turns dark red, without burning it. Take off the heat and let it cool.
Wash the mixed vegetables and boil them in a pot of water with the turmeric powder.
When the vegetables are almost done, add the tamarind paste and let it boil for a while.
Grind the roasted coconut mixture, then mix in the mashed dal.
Stir this into the pot of vegetables and let it boil for a while. Season with salt.
Fry the mustard seeds and curry leaves in a little oil until they splutter, and stir them into the sambar.
Serve hot, garnished with the coriander leaves.

recipes.title: Sev Puri
recipes.description: Crisp papdi topped with potato, tamarind and green chutneys, onion, spices and a heap of fine sev.

steps.instructionText: Arrange the papdi on a plate and make a small hole in the centre of each one.
Fill each papdi with a few cubes of boiled potato.
Add about 1/4 tsp each of tamarind chutney and coriander chutney to each one.
Sprinkle with the cumin powder, salt and red chilli powder.
Top with the onion, then sprinkle the sev generously over all the papdi.
Garnish with the coriander leaves and serve at once.

recipes.title: Seviyan Kheer (Sindhi Khirni)
recipes.description: Sindhi pudding of ghee-roasted vermicelli simmered in milk with cardamom, saffron and almonds.

steps.instructionText: Heat the ghee in a pan, add the seviyan and fry on low heat until golden brown. Take off the heat.
Bring the milk to the boil. Add the seviyan, cardamom and saffron.
Simmer until the seviyan is tender and the milk has reduced to a little over half its volume.
Mix in the sugar and boil for 5-7 minutes.
Serve garnished with the almonds.

recipes.title: Sheer Khurma
recipes.description: Eid vermicelli pudding in milk and cream, rich with ghee-fried cashews, raisins, dates and almonds.

ingredients.name: dried dates (chhuhara), soaked overnight, pitted, sliced

steps.instructionText: Heat the ghee in a large pot over low heat. Fry the cashews until browned.
Turn off the heat and add the raisins. When they swell, lift out the raisins and cashews with a spoon and set aside.
Reheat the ghee on low heat. Fry the seviyan, stirring, until golden brown; watch that it doesn't burn.
Pour in the milk and water, and return the cashews and raisins to the pot.
Add the dates and almonds and cook for about 2 minutes, until the seviyan starts to soften. Add the sugar.
Keep on low heat for 2 more minutes, then add the cream and cardamom powder.
Heat a little longer, mix well and serve hot.

recipes.title: Goan Prawn Hooman
recipes.description: Goan prawn and drumstick curry in a smooth paste of coconut, dried red chilli, turmeric and tamarind.

steps.instructionText: Put the prawns, onion, drumstick and hing in a saucepan with a little water. Cook until the prawns and drumstick are done.
Grind the coconut, dried red chillies, turmeric, peppercorns and tamarind to a fine, thick paste, adding only a tiny amount of water if needed.
Add the paste to the prawns and bring to the boil.
Add salt to taste and serve with hot white rice.

recipes.title: Sindhi Besan Mithai
recipes.description: Gram flour roasted in ghee, sweetened with sugar and topped with chopped cashews, almonds and pistachios.

steps.instructionText: Heat the ghee in a heavy pan. Add the besan and stir continuously until toasted and fragrant.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the sugar.
Return to the heat and stir until the sugar melts.
Transfer to a bowl and garnish with the cashews, almonds and pistachios.
Serve hot or cold.

recipes.title: Sindhi Pulao
recipes.description: Basmati rice cooked with deeply browned onions, green chillies, curry leaves, cashews and garam masala.

steps.instructionText: Heat some oil in a pot and fry the onions until dark brown.
Add the green chillies, curry leaves and cashews and stir for a moment.
Stir in the garam masala, black pepper, red chilli powder, bay leaf and salt.
Add the basmati rice and enough water to cook it (about 4 cups).
Simmer uncovered until all the water is absorbed and the rice is cooked. Serve hot.

recipes.title: Sindhi Tomato-Onion Raita
recipes.description: Cool curd mixed with chopped onion, tomato, green chilli and a pinch of tangy amchur.

steps.instructionText: Mix the curd, onion, green chillies, tomato, amchur and salt in a bowl.
Serve cool, as a side with rice or roti.

recipes.title: Sindhi Spiced Fish
recipes.description: Fish fillets seared on one side, then baked under a tangy curd, onion, coriander and tamarind topping.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to about 200 °C (400 °F).
Shallow fry the fish fillets in a little oil on one side only, then place them fried-side down in a baking dish.
Mix the curd, onions, coriander leaves, green chilli, dhania powder, cumin powder, salt and tamarind paste.
Spread the curd mixture over the fish and bake until golden.
Serve hot with chapatis.

recipes.title: Sindhi Vegetable Kofta
recipes.description: Fried carrot, cauliflower and potato dumplings simmered in a spiced onion and tomato gravy.

steps.instructionText: Mix the water, a pinch of salt and the cornflour into a thick batter.
Mix the carrot, cauliflower, potatoes, capsicum, green chillies, salt to taste, and half each of the black pepper and garam masala.
Wet the bread, squeeze it dry and mix it into the vegetables.
Shape into small balls and dip each one in the cornflour batter to coat well.
Fry the balls in a pan of hot oil until golden brown, then drain on paper towels.
Fry the onion in a little oil until golden brown. Add the tomatoes and fry until the oil separates.
Add a little water, salt to taste, the red chilli powder and coriander powder, and bring to the boil.
Add the fried kofta balls and simmer for a few minutes.
Take off the heat, mix in the remaining garam masala and black pepper, and serve hot with roti, naan or rice.

recipes.title: Ragi Mudde
recipes.description: Stiff finger millet balls, a rural staple of Karnataka, eaten with ghee and a thin saaru.

steps.instructionText: Bring the water to the boil in a heavy pot. Stir in a little of the ragi flour to make a paste, then add the rest of the flour.
Stir once with the handle of a wooden spoon, then leave it in the pot.
Keep on low heat for about 10 minutes, until it smells cooked.
Stir until the mixture turns dark reddish-brown and starts to leave the sides of the pot.
Take the pot off the heat and stir vigorously for 5-10 minutes; the longer you stir, the lighter the mudde.
Shape the mixture into fist-sized balls.
Serve hot: poke a hole in each ball, pour in a little ghee, and eat with a thin saaru, swallowing pieces without chewing.

recipes.title: Sylheti Beef Curry
recipes.description: Slow-simmered beef curry from Sylhet, made tangy with the wild citrus hatkora and whole spices.

steps.instructionText: Heat the vegetable oil in a large, heavy pan over medium heat.
Add the cloves, cardamom, cinnamon and bay leaves and saute for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the onions and saute until golden brown.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and saute for 2 minutes, until the raw smell goes.
Add the beef and cook until browned on all sides.
Stir in the cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric and red chilli powder and cook for 2 minutes to toast the spices.
Add the hatkora, tomatoes and green chillies and cook until the tomatoes are soft and the oil separates.
Pour in enough water to cover the beef, season with salt and bring to the boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low and simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the beef is tender.
Garnish with the coriander leaves and serve hot with steamed rice or naan.

recipes.title: Vedhmi (Puran Poli)
recipes.description: Gujarati flatbread stuffed with a sweet toor dal, jaggery and cardamom filling, brushed with ghee.

steps.instructionText: Wash the toor dal and boil it in water with 1/2 tsp of the salt until soft.
Cool slightly and drain the dal in a strainer.
Add the cardamom powder and jaggery to the dal and grind to a fine paste. If it is sticky, stir it over the heat until dry. This is the puran.
Knead the wheat flour with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and enough water into a soft dough.
Add the oil and knead again until it is absorbed.
Make an equal number of balls from the dough and the puran.
Roll out each dough ball into a small round, place a ball of puran in the centre and close the dough over it.
Roll it out again gently into a flat stuffed poli, like a stuffed paratha.
Heat a tawa (griddle) and cook each poli on both sides.
Brush both sides with the ghee and serve.

recipes.title: Dahi Chicken Curry
recipes.description: Chicken marinated in spiced yogurt, then simmered with onion, tomato, ground cashews and coconut milk.

steps.instructionText: Cut the chicken into 5-7 cm pieces and make small slashes in each with a knife.
In a large bowl, mix the garlic, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala, the cayenne, curd, coriander leaves and black pepper.
Add the chicken, coat it well and marinate in the fridge for 8 hours.
In a large pot, fry the onions, green chillies and tomato in the oil over low heat until the onions are light yellow.
Stir in the remaining salt, red chilli powder and garam masala, the curry powder and the ground cashews.
Add the chicken pieces and fry for about 5 minutes, stirring gently.
Add the leftover marinade and enough water to cover the chicken. Stir in the coconut milk, if using.
Cook over low to medium heat for 30-45 minutes, until the chicken is done.
Take off the heat and rest for a few minutes so the chicken absorbs the sauce. Serve with basmati rice.

recipes.title: Tuna Curry
recipes.description: Quick pantry curry of canned tuna and frozen vegetables in a creamy curry-powder milk sauce.

ingredients.name: frozen vegetables (carrot, green beans or peas)

steps.instructionText: Melt the butter (or heat the olive oil) in a saucepan and saute the onion until transparent.
Add the flour and stir until it is fully mixed in.
Add the curry powder and stir until it is fully mixed in.
Add the milk and frozen vegetables and stir until the mixture is hot again.
Stir in the tuna, then season with salt and black pepper; tuna is salty, so taste first.
Heat through and serve over rice.

recipes.title: Spicy Red Curry Chicken Stew
recipes.description: Chicken thighs and potatoes slow-baked with red curry paste, Thai chillies, fish sauce and tomato paste.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs, in 4 cm cubes

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 120 °C (250 °F). Dredge the chicken in the flour.
Heat the oil in a heavy ovenproof pot. Brown the chicken a few pieces at a time on all sides, then lift it out.
Saute the onion in the remaining oil until translucent and slightly browned at the edges.
Mix in the red curry paste, Thai chillies, fish sauce, chicken broth, tomato paste, potatoes and garlic.
Return the chicken to the pot, cover tightly and bake for 4 1/2 hours, until the chicken is tender.
Sprinkle the parsley over each bowl and serve warm.
